To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of graphic satire in the long nineteenth-century United Kingdom was a powerful means to communicate the transnational aspects of British life, and that the transnational nature of British graphic satire is a subject that is worthy of more sustained academic study.

1) The United Kingdom, in the long nineteenth-century, was a major global power that was represented and commented upon, often critically, by graphic satire from a range of countries; 2) Graphic satire was a transnational genre, which circulated widely throughout the period; 3) Graphic satirists were not only influenced by British graphic satire, but also responded to it; 4) The British graphic satirical corpus was not a closed canon, but a dynamic and open one;

(1) graphic satires produced in the long nineteenth-century were transnational in nature, (2) they were produced by a wide range of artists from different backgrounds, and (3) their transnational nature was influenced by the British graphic tradition, and the British graphic satirists of the period.

the ways in which the transnational is represented in graphic satires of the long nineteenth century and the ways in which it influenced the production of such imagery.
how the United Kingdom was viewed, and how it viewed itself, in graphic satires produced by a range of artists, in Britain and abroad, in the long nineteenth-century.
